Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 12/1/2022 to 1/1/2023. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2021) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, NRS Chapter 239, I request the following records regarding Chili’s Grill & Bar located at 10340 N. McCarran Blvd., Reno, NV 89503, for the period January 1, 2024, through the date this request is processed:
All routine health inspection reports, follow-up inspection reports and reinspection results.

All complaints regarding food safety, sanitation or suspected foodborne illness, including records documenting the agency’s investigation and findings. Personal identifying information about complainants may be redacted.

All notices of violation, corrective action requirements, fines, permit suspensions or closure orders.

All correspondence between the agency and restaurant representatives concerning inspection violations, complaints and corrective actions.

This request is being made by a journalism student at the University of Nevada, Reno, for noncommercial research purposes. Please notify me of any anticipated fees before incurring costs. I do not authorize fees without prior approval.

Please fulfill this request electronically, preferably as searchable PDFs, with any existing spreadsheets provided in their original electronic format.

If any portion of a record is exempt from disclosure, please release the remaining nonexempt portions and identify the legal basis for each withholding.

Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to receiving your response within the timeframe provided by law.

Sincerely,

Olivia Green

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

olivia green

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Sheriff's Department PROTECT Act Policies November 2026 (Norfolk County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1. Sheriff’s Department policies, memos or other guidance  currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:
A. Fingerprint and other data sharing with the above-named federal entities,
B. Guidance or policies concerning when communication with federal immigration authorities is allowed. This includes policies concerning how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances. This also includes how and under what circumstances department employees are to document and respond to ICE detainer requests and other requests for information.

2. All Sheriff’s Department policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of sheriff department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies concerning the use of sheriff department parking lots, facility interior, or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.  

3. All training materials the Sheriff’s Department has developed, used or trained employees on from September 4, 2026 through October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026) regarding civil immigration enforcement, communication with federal immigration authorities, or the use of Sheriff’s department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Citizens for Juvenile Justice is an independent nonprofit organization working to reform youth serving systems statewide through Massachusetts. We engage in advocacy across the Commonwealth to ensure all youth are treated fairly and equitably regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, disability or immigration status. We plan to use these records to ensure that all people in Massachusetts, including youth, are adequately protected by law enforcement agencies regardless of real or perceived immigration status.  In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.
The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,
Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initiatives 
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
